label: ai-generated
title: Taking risks

questions: Where do you live, and what do you like most about the area?
How do you usually spend your free time during the week?
Is there anything you have recently started doing for the first time?
Would you describe yourself as someone who plans ahead, or do you prefer to be spontaneous? Why?
What kind of weather puts you in a good mood?
If you could spend a year living in another country, where would you go and why?
How important is it for you to have a daily routine?

part2.instructions: Here are three situations showing people taking a risk. Choose two of them and talk about them on your own for about one minute. Compare the two situations and answer the question below. After that, your partner will answer a short question about your situations.
situations: A young woman is halfway up a steep rock face, roped to a partner below. She is reaching for the next handhold while looking down nervously.
A man in his forties stands in an empty shop he has just rented, surrounded by boxes and paint pots. He has left a secure office job to open his own cafe.
A student at an airport is hugging her parents goodbye before flying to another continent to study. Her suitcase is beside her and she looks both excited and tearful.
part2.question: Why might the people have decided to take these risks, and how might they be feeling at this moment?
part2.partnerQuestion: Which of these risks do you think would be the hardest to take? Why?

part3.question: Why do some people choose to take risks in their lives, while others prefer to play it safe?
options: the influence of family and upbringing
the desire for recognition or excitement
part3.decisionQuestion: Which of these factors do you think has the greatest influence on whether a person takes risks, and why?

questions: Do you think young people today are encouraged enough to take risks? Why or why not?
Some people say that failure is the best teacher. To what extent do you agree?
Should governments do more to protect people from the consequences of risky choices, or is that a matter of personal responsibility?
How has social media changed the kinds of risks people are willing to take?
Is it possible to become braver through practice, or is courage something people are born with?
In what situations might avoiding risk actually be the more dangerous option?
